featured_techniques.technique: Cross-training employees to service the whole lifecycle of the customer
Rebranding branches as 'stores' and designing them as community-focused spaces
Creating an ambient, multi-use customer environment (greeter, coffee bar, open computers)
Night-time, family-friendly programming with video screens for kids
Removing physical barriers (red ropes) to streamline service

sections.description: Introduces the core problem: banking was organized around internal silos that didn't account for a customer’s broader life needs, such as obtaining a mortgage while checking balances or seeking information. Sets up the transition to a life-centered approach.
sections.title: Problem framing: silos vs. life-centered banking

sections.description: Describes how Umpqua Bank reframes branches as stores designed to support the customer’s life. Highlights cross-trained staff who can assist a wide range of needs, a greeter to welcome customers, coffee bars and computer access to encourage longer visits, and after-hours family-oriented programming. The narrative notes that the environment is purposefully formed, with the removal of barriers ('red ropes') to enable service aligned with the customer’s life, and frames this approach as the driver of growth versus legacy practices.
sections.title: Umpqua Bank's life-centric store model and experiential design

summary: The video presents a case study of Umpqua Bank adopting a life-centric service model that moves beyond traditional branch silos. It describes rebranding branches as open, community-oriented 'stores' and emphasizes operational continuity through cross-training so staff can address the full spectrum of a customer's life needs. The presentation highlights several experiential elements—the greeter, coffee bars, open computer access, and night-time video screens for kids—that collectively create a welcoming, multi-use environment. A key takeaway is the deliberate removal of physical barriers (the 'red ropes') to enable a more fluid customer experience and a growth strategy grounded in serving the customer's life rather than enforcing legacy banking practices.
title: From Banking Silos to Life-Centric Stores: Umpqua Bank's Customer-Life Driven Model
